title: Arkansas floodplain disclosure law: What to know - NewsBreak
text:
By Dylan Neuner ,
4 hours ago
BENTONVILLE, Ark. (KNWA/FOX24) — According to Arkansas state law, there is no requirement for sellers to disclose floodplain information to buyers.
However, it is required for sellers to pass on information about any flood damage or prior flooding to the property.
According to the Northwest Arkansas Council, approximately 36 people are moving to the area per day. Many of those new residents are from out of state and may be unfamiliar with the state law.
Brian Buechler is a Bentonville homeowner whose mother’s home experiences flooding in the home and around the property multiple times a year.
Buechler said no flood information was given to him before buying the home.
“Nothing in the disclosures, no signs of water damage anywhere in the house. So it really does seem to be new. But since the problem started four, five, or six times a year,” Buechler said.
It’s a problem that is relatively new to Buechler, who has owned the home since 2020. He said the flooding issues began around three years ago. He believes recent changes to the infrastructure are causing the water levels to build up.
Northwest Arkansas experiences severe flash flooding Buechler said he has reached out to the city for help, but has been met with nothing of use.
“We’ve been asking the city to do for years now is figure out why the drainage easement is blocked, why it’s not draining water like it was designed to, and figure out some sort of remediation for that. But the city hasn’t been willing to do that,” Buechler said.
Even though floodplain information is not required to be disclosed, Remax real estate agent, Mike Wilson, said there are some things home buyers can ask before purchase.
“You could look at a topographical map or something like that to see where the closest drainage area, creek, or irrigation is. Because you don’t have to be close to a lake or a river for water to be a problem,” Wilson said.
Along with doing personal research, Wilson said most realtors should do the work for their clients to ensure the home is not prone to flooding.
However, if a homeowner does find themselves in a situation where flooding is persistent, Wilson said flood insurance is a must.
“I don’t think people realize the flood insurance is not a part of your typical homeowner’s policy. So, it’s something that you have to ask for specifically,” Wilson said.
